Luis (ACME-Apps): Hey team — after migrating our DB sync job to Dedicated/private in our VPC we see a lot of streaming responses getting cut mid-event. Client receives a partial chunk, then reconnects and sometimes gets duplicate text. This is causing unexpected token usage and a billing spike.

Maya (Support): Thanks for the report, Luis. Can you confirm this is only for SSE/text-stream endpoints (not normal non-streaming API calls)? Also which client lib/version are you using?

Luis (ACME-Apps): Yes only streaming (SSE). Non-stream requests fine. Using our internal node fetch wrapper (node-fetch v2) behind our corporate squid-ish proxy. Repro steps: 1) call /v1/streams with stream=true 2) after ~10-30s, connection closes with partial event (no final "data: [DONE]") 3) client auto-reconnects and gets the remainder, sometimes duplicates.

Maya (Support): Oof. Two likely buckets: (A) middleboxes/proxy buffering/chunk coalescing causing partial frames and abrupt socket close, (B) auth/session/token rotation producing mid-stream 401 and client logic re-requesting (=> duplicates). Can you share server side request id and sample SDK request headers?

Luis (ACME-Apps): Request-id: req-8f7a3c. Header snippet: ```
GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Accept: text/event-stream
User-Agent: acme-sync/1.2
Connection: keep-alive
```

Ethan (SRE): Thanks — can you also capture the final bytes from the client TCP stream (tcpdump) and the proxy access/error logs around req-8f7a3c? If the proxy is aggregating chunked frames into larger buffers and then hitting an idle timeout it can drop mid-event. Also confirm your VPC MTU (many corp VPNs set 1400).

Luis (ACME-Apps): Pasted tcpdump tail: ```
10:22:11.123456 IP client->proxy: seq=... len=512
10:22:11.223789 IP client->proxy: seq=... len=1200
10:22:11.332100 IP proxy->redwood: seq=... len=1460
10:22:21.441001 IP proxy->client FIN, ack
```
Client side shows a TCP FIN ~10s after last chunk. MTU on VM is 1400.

Maya (Support): That pattern suggests the proxy or corporate edge is reassembling and then closing the connection (FIN) without propagating proper SSE boundaries. Two actionable checks: (1) disable any proxy buffering or response body buffering for the SSE route (e.g., nginx `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";`), (2) ensure proxies forward `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and don't rewrite `Content-Type: text/event-stream` to something buffered.

Ethan (SRE): Also watch for token rotation: if the proxy injects a 401 mid-stream (maybe to refresh session), client may reconnect and re-request the same stream, producing duplicate tokens counted by billing. Check the redwood server logs around req-8f7a3c: do we show any 401 / auth failures?

ingress-bot: ctx=req-8f7a3c action=ingress-accept status=200 duration_ms=1032 backend=stream-svc node=dedicated-03

Maya (Support): From the ingress side it looks 200 -> stream started. Can you share the subsequent events? If the last log for that request is a close without `event: done` then it's likely a network-level close.

Luis (ACME-Apps): We attached the proxy logs: ```
[10:22:21] client disconnected unexpectedly: upstream returned 200 but body buffering triggered; connection timed out waiting for buffer flush
```

Ethan (SRE): Classic: buffering + idle timeout. Proxy saw small chunks, buffered them, then timed out and closed the client socket with incomplete SSE. Two mitigation paths: 1) turn off buffering for the SSE endpoint, 2) add periodic heartbeat events from server (e.g., `:
` or `data: 

`) to keep the proxy from hitting idle thresholds. Also if MTU is 1400 and you see 1460 frames, fragmentation is happening at network layer which sometimes interacts badly with middleboxes. Avoid sending huge single writes; server-side runtime can be tuned to emit smaller chunk sizes (<= 1200) so proxies don't re-chunk unpredictably.

Luis (ACME-Apps): Is there a recommended config snippet for nginx / corporate proxies to accept SSE?

Maya (Support): Example nginx config we've recommended: ```
location /v1/streams/ {
  proxy_pass http://redwood-backend;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
}
```
Also set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` from upstream if you can.

Ethan (SRE): And for corporate caching proxies like Squid/BlueCoat, look for settings to disable response buffering for `text/event-stream` or use `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform`. If your proxy still rewrites or coalesces, ask the network team to whitelist the stream route.

Luis (ACME-Apps): We changed nginx proxy_buffering off and added a simple `:
` heartbeat every 15s. Re-tested for 24h — connections no longer drop and duplicates ceased. Billing anomaly still present: we got charged for two streams for two reconnects that occurred during a previous week before the fix. Can Support help reconcile?

Maya (Support): Sorry about the billing noise. Can you share the account id and approximate timestamps of the duplicate sessions? We can open a billing ticket and correlate request IDs to token usage and apply an adjustment if duplicates were caused by broken proxy behavior.

Luis (ACME-Apps): Account: acme-12345. Approx time window: 2026-02-18 10:20-10:40 UTC. Request IDs start with req-8f7a.

Billing Bot: Created billing case BC-91234 for account acme-12345. Assigned to billing@redwood. Expected response SLA: 3 business days.

Maya (Support): Thanks — next steps for us: 1) we'll ask billing to review BC-91234 and the ingested request IDs for potential adjustment, 2) SRE recommends the nginx config change + heartbeat (which you applied and validated), 3) try to set client reconnect logic to be idempotent (replay suppression) — e.g., include a `stream-session-id` on the initial request and dedupe server-side if possible.

Ethan (SRE): If you want a short-term repro harness we can share a small node script that opens an SSE connection and forces a mid-stream FIN from a proxy to reproduce. That can help validate fixes before rolling to production.

Luis (ACME-Apps): That would be great — thanks for the quick turnaround. Appreciate the help. :raised_hands:

Maya (Support): Glad it landed. I'll follow up in the billing thread once BC-91234 has an update. If anything else pops up, @here. :eyes:
